matches.quote: Only peak values are presented. The direct signature of a current-limited superfluid would be the transmitted waveform J_T(t) just above threshold
j(Q) still has a maximum, so a depairing current still exists in a d-wave superconductor; it is not undefined.
A distribution of local critical currents, or phase slips at weak links, would give exactly the gradual, monotonic suppression seen.
The two materials are also compared at different reduced temperatures ... ideally a cleaner YBCO film or a lower temperature such as 20 to 30 K
The ~10% agreement in Fig. 5a therefore sits inside an O(1) prefactor ambiguity.
The Usadel model assumes the order parameter follows the current instantaneously. The justification given ... is circular. Gap and quasiparticle relaxation in NbN after pair breaking take ~10 ps
The closed-form estimate ... applies the clean-limit Landau criterion ħk_F v_s = Δ ... The Usadel calculation (Eqs. 27 to 29) is the appropriate dirty-limit theory.
The arguments excluding vortex effects could be made experimental ... Showing that J_c* is width-independent while J_c changes would be the most direct demonstration

notes: C10, C14, C15, C16 and C19 are graded 'partly': the review targets the same questionable claims or limitations (that gradual suppression diagnoses d-wave symmetry despite polycrystalline boundary phase slips cited on p. 10; the naive hk_F v_s = Delta criterion in Eq. 9 vs self-consistent Usadel/GL depairing; that Jc* is undefined in YBCO; analysing only pulse peaks instead of full waveforms; and YBCO only being measured at 50 K rather than 20-30 K), leading to the same fixes via closely neighbouring arguments. For C24, the review catches the Fig. S4b/S6b cross-reference typo (P17) but accepts the DC delay-time heating test.
